note: Graded vertical guard of the fast race-cue pilot and its looming TTC governor inside the obstacle stack (visual_brain --obstacle-stack on|shadow; off by default and outside the stack; --vertical-guard off removes it from the stack; shadow computes and logs it without applying it). haltere.liftoff.fast_race_cue.VerticalGuardConfig. Scale-free: it reads only the looming samples the governor already receives (below_fraction, ttc_lower = the time to contact with the surface fitted below the flight path, the alarm ttc) and the measured vertical speed; it uses no height above ground and no metric distance (the only metric bound, gentle_max_m, is a height difference measured by telemetry, as the TTC policy's climb_max_m). Generic and course-agnostic. It answers the M2 round-2 findings: on Minus Two the governor's fixed 3.5 m/s terrain climb drove brain-08 (minus-brain08-gapon-01/02) and the fast PD (minus-fast6-wall-01, sinking at 0.37 m/s from 0.7 m, below-path TTC 0.24 s) into the ~2.2 m garage ceiling; on the Straw Bale downhill (straw-brain08-04/06) the drone followed the pilot's line into a convex hill and the user asked for fewer ground touches, keeping speed and height on downhills instead of sinking into the hill; the Pine Valley mound climb (pine-fast6-ttc-01) must keep working. The values are the task's a-priori values (sink margin from full at a below-path TTC of 1.5 s to none at 0.6 s; about 1 m/s of climb without repeated rising-ground evidence) and reuse the existing declared values where one exists (level_band = the ceiling guard's overhead_min_rise 0.3 m/s; climb_on_s = the TTC policy's climb_on_s 1.2 s; arrest_acceleration = the policy's terrain_climb_acceleration 10 m/s^2; gentle_max_m = the ceiling guard's weak_climb_max_m 1 m; the climb hold, release and escalated height bound are the TTC policy's own). Version 1 was set after inspecting the anatomy of the incidents named above (logs, looming samples) and before any replay of the guard. Version 2 keeps every value and changes three rules after the open-loop replay of version 1 (see change and previous_versions), so every replayed flight is development evidence for version 2, not held-out evidence. The hash covers everything except frozen/frozen_at/sha256; a change needs a new version and a new freeze before any live flight, and every version is reported. Offline replays of this guard are open loop and are not flight evidence.

vertical_guard_notes.sink_margin: rule 1: the path's crossing TTC with the surface below it, max(alarm ttc, ttc_lower), of the latest sample that has a ttc_lower (aged by the time since its capture, kept memory_s = 1 s after its receipt) scales the pilot's own requested sink by clip((ttc - margin_zero_s) / (margin_full_s - margin_zero_s), 0, 1). Over flat ground both TTCs of a descending path are height / sink rate, so the allowed sink shrinks as the ground approaches (an approach that slows down, not a dive). A surface below the path that the path itself does not head into (a short ttc_lower with a long alarm: the lower window sees ground in front of a ring or an arch opening while the focus of expansion sees through it) limits nothing. The factor falls at up to factor_down_rate (4 /s) and recovers at up to factor_up_rate (1 /s), and the vertical command keeps the pilot's 5 m/s^2 slew, so the request changes without a jump. A requested climb is never scaled
vertical_guard_notes.keep_speed: while the guard withholds part of the pilot's sink, arrests a descent or withholds a terrain climb because the drone descends, and while the pilot's support timers run (the requested sink is not achieved and the drone rests on the terrain below: contact), the descent-path governor's shortfall is not fed, so it does not cut the horizontal request for a sink that was withheld or that the terrain prevents: the drone keeps its speed (throttle up, nose forward) and follows the terrain instead of sinking into it. The guard itself never changes the horizontal request
vertical_guard_notes.descent_first: rule 2: a below-path alarm (below_fraction >= the TTC policy's terrain_fraction 0.7, with the path's crossing TTC, max(alarm ttc, ttc_lower) aged by odometry, under climb_on_s) received while the drone descends (measured vz < -level_band) is the ground looming because the drone descends: the vertical request is held at least level (max(pilot request, 0): never a climb the pilot did not ask for) for arrest_hold_s, brought there at up to arrest_acceleration, and no climb starts. While the drone descends no terrain climb is applied at all (the climb resumes once it is level). On minus-fast6-wall-01 the governor's 3.5 m/s climb started on such a sample (below_fraction 0.78, lower TTC 0.24 s, alarm 0.71 s) while the PD sank at 0.31 m/s
vertical_guard_notes.rising_ground: rule 3: a terrain climb needs confirm (2) below-path alarms received while level or climbing within confirm_window_s (0.3 s); its rate is graded by urgency on the below-path TTC (ttc_lower aged by odometry, as the governor ages it): vertical_up (3.5 m/s) x clip((climb_on_s - ttc) / (climb_on_s - climb_full_s), 0, 1), zero at 1.2 s and full at 0.6 s (the sink margin's zero point). Until rising ground is confirmed the climb is bounded to gentle_climb (1 m/s) and to gentle_max_m (1 m) above where the episode began. Rising ground is confirmed by rising_confirm (2) below-path alarms received within rising_window_s (0.5 s) while the drone already climbs faster than rising_min_rise (0.5 m/s, half the gentle climb) and the guard's own climb is the binding vertical request (above the pilot's own request): the ground keeps looming although the guard makes the drone climb, which a floor under a sinking path or a thin structure below the path does not do. A pilot that follows a ring up a hill climbs by its own request; alarms then say nothing about the guard's climb being too slow. Then the graded rate applies up to vertical_up, bounded by the TTC policy's climb_max_m (2.5 m). The policy's climb hold (0.5 s) and release (3 m/s^2) are unchanged; so are the ceiling guard (version 3), whose overhead cut still ends any climb under overhead evidence, and its explained (lower-window only) samples, which only sustain a climb, at most gentle_climb
vertical_guard_notes.other_climbs: no other rule of the fast pilot climbs faster than about 1 m/s without the pilot's own evidence: support climb 1 m/s, search 0.5 m/s, the ceiling guard's weak climbs 1 m/s; the launch (1.5 m/s below 0.6 m) and a ring clamped at the top edge ('above', the pilot's own target above) are unchanged
vertical_guard_notes.not_used: the camera process publishes neither the upper window's TTC nor below_fraction_1side, and the logged flights do not carry them; the guard uses the published fields only. On the Straw Bale downhill spots the flight path points below the camera's field of view (looming2's focus of expansion lies below the image; every window is outside it) for the whole approach to each contact, so no looming sample carries below-path evidence there before contact (found by inspecting the offline looming samples and re-running looming2 on the recorded frames of straw-brain08-04, before any replay of this guard): this guard cannot see those contacts coming. It is reported with the replay, not worked around here

change: v2 (after the open-loop replay of v1, before any flight; every value is v1's): (1) rules 1 and 2 use the path's crossing TTC max(alarm ttc, ttc_lower) instead of ttc_lower alone: in the v1 replay of straw-brain08-04 the lower window read 0.8-1.3 s under both descending arches while the alarm read 1.8-9.9 s (the path pointed through the arch), and v1 withheld up to 1.0 m/s of the pilot's sink for about 2 s before the first arch and 0.7 m/s for about 1 s before the second, where earlier flights show the top beam only 0.3-0.5 m above clean crossings; (2) rising ground (the escalation beyond gentle_climb) needs the guard's own climb to be the binding vertical request: in the v1 replay of both Straw Bale laps the guard escalated on every uphill leg, where the pilot itself climbs 0.8-1.6 m/s toward rings up the hill, adding 3.5 m/s climbs for 55-62 s per lap (the laps flew those legs without contact); (3) keep speed also while the pilot's support timers run (contact): in the v1 replay the descent-path governor still cut the horizontal request to 0.44-0.53 during every Straw Bale contact, because the looming samples there carry no below-path evidence. Every other rule and value is v1's.
